intro: Milan spent nearly six centuries building its cathedral, and it shows: 135 spires, 3,400 statues, and a golden Virgin on top. This is the story of the Duomo, the church that took longer to finish than most empires lasted.
page_title: Milan Cathedral: Exploded 3D Model and History | Architectural Atlas

sections.body: In 1386, Gian Galeazzo Visconti, the ruler consolidating his grip on Milan, laid the first stone of a cathedral meant to modernize the city and celebrate his expanding territory. The project, run by the Fabbrica del Duomo, the cathedral works, would outlive him by nearly six centuries: architects, sculptors and artisans came and went, styles shifted from French Gothic to Renaissance to Neoclassical, and the building absorbed them all. Leonardo da Vinci submitted drawings. Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the work completed. The final details were finished in 1965, 579 years after the start. Few buildings on Earth were under construction longer.
sections.heading: Six centuries, one church

sections.body: The cathedral is 158.6 meters long and 92 meters wide, the largest church in Italy and among the largest in the world, with room for 40,000 people. Its core is brick, but everything the eye touches is Candoglia marble, quarried in the Ossola valley since 1387 and floated down canals to Milan. Inside, five naves run the length of the church on four rows of 52 columns. The building follows the Ambrosian Rite of Milan rather than the Roman one, and it is dedicated to St Mary of the Nativity, Santa Maria Nascente, which is why the Virgin, not a male saint, rules the skyline.
sections.heading: A mountain of marble

sections.body: What makes the Duomo unforgettable is its roofline: a forest of 135 spires, each carrying statues, rising above more than 3,400 sculptures and 96 gargoyles that spit rainwater clear of the marble. The tallest spire reaches 108.5 meters, and on it stands the Madonnina, the little Madonna: a gilded copper statue of the Virgin Mary placed in 1774 and sheathed in gold leaf. For almost two centuries she was the highest point in Milan, and by unwritten law nothing in the city could rise above her. Taller buildings eventually did, but the Madonnina never lost her place as the city's protector.
sections.heading: A forest of spires

sections.body: The west front faces the Piazza del Duomo, the square from which Milan's streets radiate, with five bronze doors opening onto it. The facade is the cathedral's public face: colossal, theatrical, almost flamboyantly Gothic, the backdrop for everything from political rallies to fashion week. Below it lies the crypt and the remains of earlier churches, including the 5th-century basilica of St Ambrose. The Duomo is not just a church in Milan; it is the point the whole city is organized around.
sections.heading: The facade that faces the piazza

sections.body:
Vittorio De Sica gave the cathedral its most magical screen moment. In Miracle in Milan (1951), the homeless community of the shantytown, rounded up by police in the Piazza del Duomo, escapes on broomsticks made to fly by Toto's last wish. They circle the cathedral and soar over its spires toward a land where, as Toto says, good morning really means good morning. The cathedral is the film's final backdrop and the symbol of the miracle in the title.

The building keeps collecting cameras. During the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics, the cathedral stood at the center of the broadcast: promos and intros framed it as the jewel of the host city, and an NBC segment narrated by Stanley Tucci took viewers inside to argue that the city radiates outward from this single monument. Six centuries after the first stone, the Duomo still opens every montage of Milan.

timeline.text: Gian Galeazzo Visconti lays the first stone; the Fabbrica del Duomo begins nearly six centuries of work.
The gilded Madonnina is placed on the main spire at 108.5 meters.
Vittorio De Sica's Miracle in Milan premieres; its finale flies over the cathedral.
The final details are completed, 579 years after construction began.
A major restoration of the cathedral is completed.
The Milano Cortina Winter Olympics put the cathedral at the center of the world broadcast.
